title: Looking for movies (or any media) that would somehow explore the dawn of human consciousness or simply be set tens of thousands of years ago and portraying very early men.

commenti.body:
Always felt like a B movie from afar but I'll probably watch it.  
I also forgot to mention that I have a -20 000 BC fantasm with european tundra and doggerland and shit.

Try 2001 A Space Odyssey. It has an interesting exploration of early man and the development of consciousness. 

For comment length requirements, I have decided to provide a ChatGPT generated synopsis of 2001:

2001 A Space Odyssey" est fabula sci-fi quae initium habet in praehistoria, ubi monolithus ex alienigenis homines ad evolutionem impellit. Per evolutionem, homines ad spatium navigandum perveniunt, ubi monolithus iterum apparet. In fine, astronauta Dave Bowman, inter actionem cum monolitho, ad metam transcendentem pervenit et novam formam vitae attingit.

While not on the timescale you're looking for, Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner does tell a pre-modern story set entirely in a hunter-gatherer society--so at least a similar subsistence strategy. Movies like Quest for Fire and Clan of the Cave Bear may be *set* in the paleolithic, but the story they tell is still very accessible and feels natural to Western audiences. Atanarjuat was interesting to me because it is based on a very old oral tradition and is from an indigenous perspective. So it felt different.

> \-20 000 BC fantasm with european tundra and doggerland and shit.

wut

On the Silver Globe, which I wrote about on here a couple of days ago, shows the beginning of a completely new society on a new world. This isn't necessarily the main thrust of the film, but it definitely provokes a lot of thought around this topic.

There was a 2018 animated film called Alpha. I wanted to see it as soon as I found out about it, since it imagines a subject I’ve often wondered about - the first domestication of wolves by early humans. It’s not bad for an animated film that has no words, and the research they put into it really shows in the skin clothing they wear, the landscape, the hunting tools etc.  Although I think I remember an anthropologist saying that the way the wolf becomes domesticated- the wolf is injured and mistrustful of the young human who nurses it back to health - was probably not the way this happened. In reality dogs more likely chose to be around humans of their own free will.   
(Apparently during the making of this film, the working title was The Solutrean. This is the name given to a Paleolithic hunting culture 20,000 years ago)
